clue.text: Ticket for the soldier?

parts.note: read 'ticket' as a little tick, the mark a teacher puts by a correct answer, and ask what soldier's title fits that mark

explanation.surface: Someone asks which pass or permit a serving soldier needs.
explanation.walkthrough: A tick marks something as correct, so it is literally a mark for 'right'. In drill, the soldier who stands at the right of the front rank, for the others to line up on, has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: In military drill this is the soldier placed on the right flank as the guide the rank dresses by.

clue.text: Inches which may cover large area

definitions.text: Inches which may cover large area

parts.words: Inches which may cover large area
parts.note: inch is a Scots word for a small island, and a group of such islands can spread over a wide stretch of sea

explanation.surface: A measurement of a few inches somehow spreads over a large area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inches' looks like a unit of length, but in Scotland an inch is a small island (Inchcolm, Inchkeith).
explanation.definitionFit: Inch is the Scottish word for a small island, so inches are small islands.

clue.text: Marx on cause of death

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers, the silent one with the harp
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment on what a Marx (Karl, presumably) said about mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' suggests Karl, but it is Harpo of the Marx Brothers comedy team.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler's barbed spear is what kills the whale, a weapon and so a cause of death.

clue.text: Heaps of earth cover untidy son with mud

indicators.note: an untidy heap has its contents jumbled, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Muddy piles of soil end up all over a messy boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges SON plus MUD together; 'cover' and 'with' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hills or banks of piled-up soil are this, as in burial barrows.

clue.text: Kind of university for stalwart of the left?

definitions.meaning: a civic British university founded in the late 19th or early 20th century, built of the material, as opposed to Oxford and Cambridge
a solid building block of the left wing: a socialist (red) who is a brick, that is a reliable good sort

explanation.surface: Which university suits a loyal socialist?
explanation.walkthrough: British 'red-brick' universities are the Victorian civic ones such as Manchester and Leeds. 'A brick' is old British slang for a dependable person, and 'red' means left-wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic universities such as Leeds are so called from their building material; a staunch socialist is a reliable red, a 'brick'.

clue.text: Something on the head which makes the listener panic

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
a flap is a state of panic or agitation

explanation.surface: A hat or noise that sends whoever hears it into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listener' looks like a person; it is the organ itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap's side flap that folds down to keep the ear warm is worn on the head.

clue.text: They provide close-up views of sport and show great sides sin inordinately

definitions.text: They provide close-up views of sport and show

indicators.note: inordinately means beyond proper order, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Front-row places at a boxing match reveal every great flank and excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinately' rearranges GREAT, SIDES and SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Places right beside a boxing ring or circus ring give spectators the closest view of the action.

clue.text: Help of a calm sort given under a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed below the first

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
staid means sober and calm in manner

explanation.surface: Peaceful assistance found beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'given under' puts STAID below FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency treatment for the injured is immediate help before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Examination enables one to lay out on a single detention

parts.note: to lay out money is to invest it
I is the Roman numeral one
gating is confining a student to college, a school or university detention

explanation.surface: A claim that inquiry lets someone set out a lone punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Gating is British school and college slang for being kept in as a punishment. 'enables one to' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking into a matter closely is an inquiry or examination.

clue.text: The sluggard goes back in when the quarrel dies back

indicators.note: goes back says the letters found are read backwards
in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lazy man returns home once the row finally fizzles out.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'goes back in when' as definition, but the sluggard alone is the lazy person; 'goes back' reverses and 'in' marks letters inside 'quarrel dies'. RELDI reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluggard is a lazy person who does no work.

clue.text: Put one's name at the bottom using the right end freely

definitions.text: Put one's name at the bottom

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters move loosely into a new order

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Signing off using the right-hand end of the page without restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges USING, R and END.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign a document is to write your signature beneath its text.

clue.text: Its contents are lethal and wound a veteran

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
an older man is a veteran in years

explanation.surface: A deadly container, and an old soldier injured.
explanation.walkthrough: A gas holder (gasometer) is the large tank that stores town gas, which was poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer stores fuel gas, which is poisonous to breathe.

clue.text: The yarn in full is less amusing

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A long story told in full is less entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a tall tale; it is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings, a type of yarn.

clue.text: Having no coastline, the country has lost its capital

indicators.note: a word's capital is its first letter, here removed from the country name

parts.note: Finland is a Nordic country

explanation.surface: A landlocked nation whose capital city has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Helsinki but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A place away from the sea, with no shore, lies in the interior.

clue.text: In distinctive clothing, so survived without anger arising

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the second piece is surrounded

parts.note: to have lived is to have survived

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Dressed in uniform, someone got through life without losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. 'arising' turns IRE upward to ERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Servants dressed in a household's uniform, its livery, are wearing distinctive dress.

clue.text: Frost producer growing in the garden?

definitions.text: Frost producer growing in the garden?

parts.words: Frost producer growing in the garden?
parts.note: read 'frost producer' as a factory making ice, then as something growing in a garden whose leaves look frosted

explanation.surface: Something that brings frost is sprouting among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: A factory that makes ice and a succulent whose leaves glisten as if frosted share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigeration works makes frozen water, and a succulent garden plant with glistening leaves shares the name.

clue.text: What is very fine gives encouragement over unpleasant experience

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
a hellish time is a hell

explanation.surface: Something excellent gives support after a dreadful ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very fine' means delicate and thin, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer casing of a hen's product is extremely thin and fragile.

clue.text: Imagine one snag with Eve being corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted text is garbled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Picture the snag as Eve is led astray, as in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being corrupted' rearranges I, SNAG and EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in the mind is to imagine it.

clue.text: Withdraw /although not handicapped

definitions.meaning: to pull an entrant out of a race or contest
in golf, a player receiving no handicap allowance

explanation.surface: Pulling out even though nothing held you back.
explanation.walkthrough: A scratch golfer plays off a handicap of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrants removed from a race are struck off the list; a zero-handicap golfer plays level.

clue.text: One animal reveals the reverse of poetry in another

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the pig is another animal

indicators.note: the reverse of means the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: One creature exposes the back of a verse in another.
explanation.walkthrough: A pye-dog is an ownerless stray dog of India and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A pye-dog is a stray, half-wild dog, so one animal.

clue.text: He does not believe it is fashionable to change the field

parts.note: in means trendy

indicators.note: to change the word is to alter the order of its letters

explanation.surface: An unbeliever says it is trendy to switch fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges FIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without religious faith, in the eyes of believers, is an unbeliever.

clue.text: Order makes man lose a hundred with poor quality goods

indicators.note: lose means the letter is dropped

parts.note: Dick is a man's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
tat is shoddy stuff

explanation.surface: An order forces a trader to give up a hundred along with cheap rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' removes C from DICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree imposed by authority without consultation is an order.

clue.text: If the mistakes were pointless there would be nothing in school subjects

definitions.text: If the mistakes were pointless there would be nothing in school subjects

parts.words: If the mistakes were pointless there would be nothing in school subjects
parts.note: take compass points off the plural word for mistakes and what is left is a zero inside the three Rs

explanation.surface: A teacher's grumble: without the mistakes, the curriculum would be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E and S (compass points) from ERRORS to get RROR: O (nothing) in RRR, the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is a slip or blunder.

clue.text: Mean fellow given cover by a stone

parts.note: skin covers the body
flint is a hard stone

explanation.surface: A stingy man is shielded by a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' is stingy, not cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser so stingy he would skin a flint is a mean fellow.

clue.text: Figures of those not in favour of following one

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the cons are the arguments against

explanation.surface: Numbers of those opposed coming after one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts CONS after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious images or emblematic figures are images, as in Orthodox painting.

clue.text: Attention needed by team wrecked in river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Trent is a river of the English Midlands

indicators.note: wrecked means broken up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A side ruined on the river needs medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges TEAM to ATME inside TRENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to a patient is attention.

clue.text: Go under with the Central Line

definitions.text: Go under with the Central Line

parts.words: Go under with the Central Line
parts.note: the Central Line is a London Underground line, so travelling on it means going under, here read as sinking below water

explanation.surface: Travelling underground on one of London's tube lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central Line is a London Underground route; 'go under' is to sink and die in water.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink beneath water and perish is to go under.

clue.text: Hobby enthusiast has a letter with a recent catalogue

parts.note: phi is a Greek letter
late means recent, as in the late news
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A collector owns a letter and the latest catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is a Greek letter, though the stamp collector suggests a posted one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp collector pursues one of the classic pastimes.
